title: The Water Palace of Five Colors Legend
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Yokomizo -- the regional police inspector who recurs across the Suzuki/Nagano arcs the way Megure recurs in Tokyo -- ) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved (person/location/object). The old wiki-summary case file (cases/ep210-211_...json) had the correct culprit (Yakura) and victim (the headmaster) identity, so label.murderer_id is unchanged, but it collapsed the whole crime into three generic events and one clue, missed the headmaster's backstory (his late wife, the succession plan he was about to announce, the burned fishing rods), missed both red-herring suspects' actual motives and cleared alibis (Mimura's rival-teacup errand, Ryoichi's resentment over the succession/fishing rods, Hanasaki accused by Mimura), and understated the mechanism: the murder was a stabbing on the veranda followed by strangulation with a rope tied in a fisherman's Cleat Hitch knot, staged as a failed suicide attempt then a hanging, with the body dragged onto the beam and the door self-locked by a timer-driven waterwheel mechanism combined with a thumbtack/rubber-band door-spring trick -- not simply 'a knot and a waterwheel'. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Location/lock contradiction: a blood trail runs from the veranda into the tea room, consistent with a failed wrist-cutting suicide attempt outside before hanging inside -- but both the entrance door and the water-room door were found locked from the inside. A wounded man stumbling in after failing to kill himself outside could not have secured the door behind him, revealing the 'suicide' as staged.

Beam-mark comparison: the ceiling beam shows a fresh, sharp rope groove that is invisible from a distance in the tea room's dim light but visible close-up, alongside wood splinters freshly scattered on the tatami -- proving the beam had been used to hoist a weight only minutes before discovery, not hours earlier as the staged suicide-by-hanging timeline required.
